# doc-html-translate command line

Command set 1.0 of `doc-html-translate.exe`. Scripts and agents drive the product by its command line. This page is rendered from the manifest [`cli-commands.json`](cli-commands.json), and `doc-html-translate.exe commands --json` prints the same manifest as data (APP-COMMANDS rules 18 and 20).

The grammar is APP-COMMANDS rules 1 and 3: a verb of one or two lower-case words, then options written `--name`, `--name=value` or `--name value`; `--` ends the options; verbs and options are compared without regard to case, values never. An unknown verb, an unknown option, a missing value or a value of the wrong kind exits 10 and runs nothing. A command line is at most 64 KiB and one argument at most 32 KiB; more is refused, never cut.

The conversion call `doc-html-translate.exe [flags] <path>` keeps its own flags and exit codes: [`../README.md`](../README.md) lists the flags and `OCR-INVOCATION` section D the exit codes.

Print the list of commands this product accepts.

```text
doc-html-translate commands [--json] [--result <path>]
```

- **Risk:** `safe` - **cold start:** `oneshot` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** 5000 ms - **idempotent:** yes - **since:** 1.0
- **Forward:** `never` (the process that receives the command does the work itself)
- **Frozen aliases:** `-h` `-help` `--help`

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | bool | no | `false` | Print the manifest itself as JSON. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the manifest as one JSON file, written whole. |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | printed |
| 1 | the result file could not be written |
| 10 | unknown option, a value of the wrong kind, or a command line over the size bound |

Examples:

```powershell
& .\doc-html-translate.exe commands --json | ConvertFrom-Json
```


Both doc-html-translate.exe and doc-html-ui.exe answer this verb from their own copy of the manifest, before any window, setting, worker or log is touched. -h, -help and --help keep printing the flag usage of the conversion call, and the readable list of this verb begins with that same block.

## `status`

Say whether the launcher is running and ready to take commands.

```text
doc-html-translate status [--json] [--result <path>]
```

- **Risk:** `safe` - **cold start:** `refuse` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** 2000 ms - **idempotent:** yes - **since:** 1.0
- **Forward:** `always` (forwarded to the running first instance over the local command pipe)

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | bool | no | `false` | Print the response line itself. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the response data as one JSON file, written whole. |

Data:

| Key | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | string | the running launcher's version |
| `pid` | int | its process id |
| `windowOpen` | bool | whether its window is on the screen right now |
| `activeRuns` | int | conversions the window has running |
| `acceptsRestrictedCommands` | bool | always false: this product has no setting of rule 13 (safe launcher verbs are always accepted; forward:never verbs are not gated) |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | running and ready |
| 2 | the running copy is older than the request's schema, or did not answer in time |
| 10 | unknown option, a value of the wrong kind, or a command line over the size bound |
| 11 | not running (reason not-running), or busy (reason busy) |
| 12 | the running copy runs elevated and the caller does not (reason elevation) |

Examples:

```powershell
& .\doc-html-translate.exe status --json | ConvertFrom-Json
```

Expected: exit 0 with version, pid, windowOpen, activeRuns while the launcher runs; exit 11 (not-running) otherwise

```cmd
doc-html-translate.exe status
```

Expected: exit 0 when running, 11 when not running

Both executables forward this verb to the running launcher over the local command pipe. With no launcher running it exits 11 (reason not-running) and starts nothing.

```text

```

- **Risk:** `safe` - **cold start:** `start` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** 10000 ms - **idempotent:** yes - **since:** 1.0

- **Forward:** `always` (forwarded to the running first instance over the local command pipe)
- **Default verb of `doc-html-ui.exe`:** a command line with no verb word, a path and flags, is this verb

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--in` | path | yes | - | A document to queue; may repeat. A relative path is resolved against the caller's working directory. |

| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the response data as one JSON file, written whole. |

Data:

| Key | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | queued |
| 1 | the result file could not be written, or the server could not start |
| 2 | the running copy is older or did not answer in time |
| 10 | no --in given, unknown option, a value of the wrong kind, or a command line over the size bound |


The bare call doc-html-ui.exe <path> that the MSIX file association and shortcuts use is this verb (defaultFor). Nothing is converted: the person starts the run in the window. Served by doc-html-ui.exe only.

## `convert`

Convert one document into clean local HTML, optionally translating it.

```text
doc-html-translate convert <path> [options] [--result <path>]
```

- **Risk:** `leaves-machine` - **cold start:** `oneshot` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** none of its own - **idempotent:** yes - **since:** 1.0
- **Forward:** `never` (the process that receives the command does the work itself)
- **Default verb of `doc-html-translate.exe`:** a command line with no verb word, a path and flags, is this verb

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<path>` | path | yes | - | The document (one per run): .epub .pdf .txt .md .fb2 .rtf .html .htm .mobi .azw3 .cbz .cbr .cb7 .cbt, a still image, or a .fd-sec secret file. |
| `--notranslate` | bool | no | `false` | Convert only, skip translation. |
| `--google` | bool | no | `false` | Translate with Google Cloud Translation; the text is sent to Google. The verb requires --max-cost with it. |
| `--ollama (alias -free)` | bool | no | `false` | Translate with the local Ollama server. |
| `--ollama-model` | string | no | `"gemma3:12b"` | Ollama model name. |
| `--ollama-parallel` | int | no | `1` | Concurrent batch requests; a value below 1 is raised to 1 with a notice. |
| `--ollama-ctx` | int | no | `8192` | Context window in tokens; a value below 512 is raised to 512 with a notice. |
| `--src` | string | no | `"en"` | Source language code. |
| `--dst` | string | no | `"ru"` | Target language code. |
| `--max-cost` | string | no | `"0"` | Positive finite USD amount: the guard and the approval for a paid run. 0 means no limit, which the verb refuses together with --google; a negative, NaN or infinite value exits 10. |
| `--ocr` | bool | no | `false` | Recognize text inside document images and overlay it as translatable HTML (needs Tesseract). |
| `--ocr-lang` | string | no | - | Recognition language(s), for example eng or eng+rus; default is --src, else eng. |
| `--multipage` | bool | no | `false` | Write one page per chapter with a table of contents instead of the single page. |
| `--split` | int | no | `5000` | Split pages at N characters for the browser's translation (0 disables). |
| `--toc-depth` | int | no | `0` | Nesting depth of the table of contents on index.html (0 = unlimited). |
| `--folder` | path | no | - | Output folder; default is beside the input. A caller that reads the result passes a fresh, empty folder (OCR-INVOCATION B2). |
| `--force` | bool | no | `false` | Rebuild even when a finished, current result exists; the converter only ever rebuilds a folder that carries its own record. |
| `--noopen` | bool | no | `false` | Do not open the browser afterwards; scripts always pass it (OCR-INVOCATION B1). |
| `--ui-lang` | enum: en ru uk de it es fr pt ar hi bn ur zh | no | - | Language of the console text and of the converted page's navigation; default is the Windows UI language. |
| `--fdsec-password-env` | string | no | - | For a .fd-sec input: the NAME of an environment variable that holds its password, never the password. Without it the verb refuses (10) instead of asking. |
| `--v` | bool | no | `false` | Verbose output. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the response data as one JSON file, written whole. |

Data:

| Key | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `outcome` | string | converted, translated, partial, skipped (translation asked for and not run: no key, estimate above --max-cost) or reused |
| `outputDir` | path | the output folder; its entry file is index.html |
| `entryFile` | path | index.html inside outputDir |
| `translation` | string | none, full or partial, as the record says |
| `complete` | object | the complete member of .doc-html-translate.json (completed, toolVersion, options, ocrForced, translation) |
| `exitCode` | int | the process exit code, repeated for a reader of the file |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | done: converted, fully translated, translation skipped, or reused |
| 1 | bad arguments or a missing input; nothing was written |
| 2 | I/O error, the output is locked by another conversion, or the result file could not be written; incomplete |
| 3 | the input could not be read or parsed, a missing Calibre or 7-Zip included; incomplete |
| 4 | translation failed, stopped part-way or could not start; the book is still produced |
| 10 | usage: unknown option, --google without a positive --max-cost, a .fd-sec input without --fdsec-password-env |
| 130 | stopped with Ctrl+C; incomplete, the next run rebuilds it |

Examples:

```powershell
& .\doc-html-translate.exe convert C:\books\a.epub --noopen --folder C:\out\job1 --result C:\out\job1.json; $LASTEXITCODE
```

Expected: 0; C:\out\job1 holds one folder with index.html and .doc-html-translate.json; job1.json names it

```cmd
doc-html-translate.exe -noopen -folder C:\out\job2 C:\books\a.epub
```

Expected: the same conversion by the frozen bare call; the same exit code and the same output

```powershell
& .\doc-html-translate.exe convert .\scan.pdf --noopen --ocr --ocr-lang eng --google --max-cost 2
```

Expected: 0 within the USD 2 guard; 4 when translation is unavailable

```powershell
& .\doc-html-translate.exe convert .\a.epub --google --noopen; $LASTEXITCODE
```

Expected: 10; the message names --max-cost, nothing was converted

The exit table is OCR-INVOCATION section D, copied. The bare call doc-html-translate.exe [flags] <path> is this verb (defaultFor): it keeps the browser opening unless --noopen, the cost dialog, the password prompt and the pause for Enter after an error, none of which the verb ever does (rule 4). Several documents: one run per document. Only doc-html-translate.exe serves this verb; doc-html-ui.exe says so and exits 10.

## `output status`

Say whether a finished result exists for a document and whether the options asked for now would reuse it.

```text
doc-html-translate output status --in <path> [--folder <dir>] [result-shaping options] [--json] [--result <path>]
```

- **Risk:** `reads-user-data` - **cold start:** `oneshot` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** 5000 ms - **idempotent:** yes - **since:** 1.0
- **Forward:** `never` (the process that receives the command does the work itself)

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--in` | path | yes | - | The document whose result is asked about. |
| `--folder` | path | no | - | The output folder the conversion used. |
| `--notranslate` | bool | no | `false` | As convert: the options whose reuse is checked. |
| `--google` | bool | no | `false` | As convert. |
| `--ollama` | bool | no | `false` | As convert. |
| `--ollama-model` | string | no | `"gemma3:12b"` | As convert. |
| `--src` | string | no | `"en"` | As convert. |
| `--dst` | string | no | `"ru"` | As convert; it shapes the result only when an engine is asked for. |
| `--ocr` | bool | no | `false` | As convert. |
| `--ocr-lang` | string | no | - | As convert. |
| `--multipage` | bool | no | `false` | As convert. |
| `--split` | int | no | `5000` | As convert. |
| `--toc-depth` | int | no | `0` | As convert. |
| `--json` | bool | no | `false` | Print the data as one JSON object. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the data as one JSON file, written whole. |

Data:

| Key | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exists` | bool | a result that the converter owns exists for this input |
| `complete` | bool | its record carries complete |
| `stale` | bool | a run with the options asked for now would rebuild it |
| `reason` | string | why it would rebuild: no-record, source-changed, options-changed, partial or untranslated; absent when current |
| `outputDir` | path | the output folder when exists |
| `entryFile` | path | index.html inside it |
| `translation` | string | none, full or partial |
| `toolVersion` | string | the version that wrote it |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | answered, including exists:false |
| 1 | the status could not be read, or the result file could not be written |
| 10 | no --in given, an unknown option, or a value the converter refuses |
| 11 | the input file does not exist |

Examples:

```powershell
(& .\doc-html-translate.exe output status --in C:\books\a.epub --json | ConvertFrom-Json).stale
```

Expected: False when a finished result matches; True with a reason when a run would rebuild it, for example after the same input is asked for with another --dst and an engine

Without --json the data is printed as key: value lines. A folder that merely holds an index.html, a saved website or the user's own, is not a result: exists is false. The same code answers the app's window, so the two cannot disagree. Only doc-html-translate.exe serves this verb.

## `doctor`

Say what this machine can do: which helper tools are found, which formats and OCR languages work.

```text
doc-html-translate doctor [--ollama [--ollama-model <m>]] [--json] [--result <path>]
```

- **Risk:** `safe` - **cold start:** `oneshot` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** 10000 ms - **idempotent:** yes - **since:** 1.0
- **Forward:** `never` (the process that receives the command does the work itself)

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--ollama` | bool | no | `false` | Also ask the local Ollama server whether it answers and has the model. Without it nothing is requested from any service. |
| `--ollama-model` | string | no | `"gemma3:12b"` | The model --ollama looks for. |
| `--json` | bool | no | `false` | Print the data as one JSON object. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the data as one JSON file, written whole. |

Data:

| Key | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | string | this build's version |
| `packaged` | bool | running from an MSIX package |
| `tools` | object | tesseract, pdftotext, calibre, sevenzip and filedo, each with found (bool) and version (string, empty when the tool reports none); never a path |
| `formats` | array | each input format: ext, tool (the helper it cannot be read without, empty for none), ready (that helper is found) and, when there is one, optionalTool (a helper that only improves the result) |
| `ocrLangs` | array | the installed recognition language codes |
| `googleKeyPresent` | bool | a Google API key is stored; the key itself is never returned |
| `ollama` | object | model, reachable (the server answered) and modelPresent; present only with --ollama |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | answered, whatever was found |
| 1 | the result file could not be written |
| 10 | unknown option, a value of the wrong kind, or a command line over the size bound |

Examples:

```powershell
(& .\doc-html-translate.exe doctor --json | ConvertFrom-Json).tools.calibre.found
```

Expected: True or False; False means .mobi and .azw3 documents are not ready to convert here

```cmd
doc-html-translate.exe doctor --ollama --json
```

Expected: exit 0; the object also has an ollama member with reachable and modelPresent

This is the machine-readable capabilities query that OCR-INVOCATION section H.1 left open. It reports booleans, version numbers, extensions and language codes only - never a path, a document name or the Google key - and writes nothing. Without --ollama nothing is requested from any service; with it, one request goes to the local Ollama server and to no other. A tool's version is the number its own version query prints; FileDO has no such query and the pdftotext carried inside this program is not unpacked to be asked, so those two report an empty version. Without --json the data is printed as key: value lines. Both doc-html-translate.exe and doc-html-ui.exe answer this verb.


- **Risk:** `reads-user-data` - **cold start:** `oneshot` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** 10000 ms - **idempotent:** yes - **since:** 1.0
- **Forward:** `never` (the process that receives the command does the work itself)

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--in` | path | yes | - | The document to check. |
| `--google` | bool | no | `false` | Check that a Google key is stored; it wins over --ollama. |
| `--ollama` | bool | no | `false` | Check that the local Ollama answers and has the model. |
| `--ollama-model` | string | no | `"gemma3:12b"` | The model --ollama looks for. |
| `--ocr` | bool | no | `false` | Check that Tesseract and the language data are present. |
| `--ocr-lang` | string | no | - | The recognition language(s) to check; default is --src, else eng. |
| `--src` | string | no | `"en"` | Source language, which --ocr falls back to. |
| `--json` | bool | no | `false` | Print the data as one JSON object. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the data as one JSON file, written whole. |

Data:

| Key | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | string | ready, optional (something is missing that only improves the result) or action (the run would fail or degrade) |
| `issues` | array | each: code, level (action or optional) and, when there is one, detail |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | answered; state says whether a run would work |
| 1 | the result file could not be written |
| 10 | no --in given, an unknown option, or a value the converter refuses |
| 11 | the file does not exist (reason target-missing) |

Examples:

```powershell
(& .\doc-html-translate.exe input check --in C:\books\a.mobi --json | ConvertFrom-Json).state
```

Expected: action when Calibre is not found, with an issue whose code is calibre

The same check answers the app's window, so the two cannot disagree. A folder, an empty file or a file that cannot be read is state action with the issue input (exit 0); only a path that does not exist exits 11. The options are read by the converter's own parser, so the defaults are the converter's. Without --json the data is printed as key: value lines. Both doc-html-translate.exe and doc-html-ui.exe answer this verb.

## `ocr langs`

List the recognition languages that are installed and the ones that can be downloaded.

```text
doc-html-translate ocr langs [--json] [--result <path>]
```

- **Risk:** `safe` - **cold start:** `oneshot` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** 5000 ms - **idempotent:** yes - **since:** 1.0
- **Forward:** `never` (the process that receives the command does the work itself)
- **Frozen aliases:** `-ocr-langs`

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | bool | no | `false` | Print the data as one JSON object. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the data as one JSON file, written whole. |

Data:

| Key | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `languages` | array | each language of the catalogue: code, name and installed (bool) |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | listed |
| 1 | the result file could not be written |
| 10 | unknown option, a value of the wrong kind, or a command line over the size bound |

Examples:

```powershell
(& .\doc-html-translate.exe ocr langs --json | ConvertFrom-Json).languages | Where-Object installed
```

Expected: the installed languages, one object each

```cmd
doc-html-translate.exe -ocr-langs
```

Expected: the listing exactly as before; it is not part of a job (OCR-INVOCATION section F)

Without --json this prints the listing that -ocr-langs prints: the tessdata folders, then one line per language (the frozen spelling, as always, first prints the one timestamped line that begins every converter run). The data names no folder. Both doc-html-translate.exe and doc-html-ui.exe answer the verb; the frozen spelling -ocr-langs is the converter's.

## `ocr download`

Download one recognition language pack into the per-user folder.

```text
doc-html-translate ocr download --lang <code> [--json] [--result <path>]
```

- **Risk:** `leaves-machine` - **cold start:** `oneshot` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** 600000 ms - **idempotent:** yes - **since:** 1.0
- **Forward:** `never` (the process that receives the command does the work itself)
- **Frozen aliases:** `-ocr-download`

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--lang` | string | yes | - | A catalogue code, for example rus (ocr langs lists them); the pack is checked against its pinned digest. |
| `--json` | bool | no | `false` | Print the data as one JSON object. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the data as one JSON file, written whole. |

Data:

| Key | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lang` | string | the code |
| `installed` | bool | true when the pack is in place, which it always is for exit 0 |
| `downloaded` | bool | false when the verified pack was already there and nothing was fetched |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | installed, or already installed |
| 1 | the download or its verification failed, or the result file could not be written |
| 10 | a code that is not in the catalogue (the sentence names the catalogue), no --lang, an unknown option or a value of the wrong kind |

Examples:

```powershell
& .\doc-html-translate.exe ocr download --lang rus --json; $LASTEXITCODE
```

Expected: 0 and installed:true; downloaded is false when the pack was already there

```cmd
doc-html-translate.exe -ocr-download rus
```

Expected: exit 0; the frozen spelling prints its progress as before, and exits 1 for an unknown code

The one request goes to the Tesseract project's public tessdata_fast repository and names one catalogue file; no user content leaves the machine. timeoutMs is the download client's own limit. The frozen spelling -ocr-download <code> keeps exit 1 for an unknown code; the verb answers 10, a wrong value (rule 3). Served by doc-html-translate.exe only.

## `report build`

Pack the recent run logs and an environment summary into one archive for the author.

```text
doc-html-translate report build [--out <path>] [--overwrite] [--json] [--result <path>]
```

- **Risk:** `writes-user-data` - **cold start:** `oneshot` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** 30000 ms - **idempotent:** no - **since:** 1.0
- **Forward:** `never` (the process that receives the command does the work itself)
- **Frozen aliases:** `-report`

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--out` | path | no | - | The archive or folder to write; default is the reports folder under the app's data folder. A folder (existing, or ending in a separator) receives the file named by DIAGNOSTIC-REPORT section 8 item A; a missing folder is refused (exit 11, reason target-missing) and never created. An existing target file is refused (exit 11, reason exists) without --overwrite. |
| `--overwrite` | bool | no | `false` | Replace an existing target file, whole. It skips only the refusal of an existing file. |
| `--json` | bool | no | `false` | Print the data as one JSON object. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the data as one JSON file, written whole. |

Data:

| Key | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | path | the archive |
| `droppedLogs` | int | older logs that did not fit and were left out |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | written |
| 1 | the archive could not be built, or the result file could not be written |
| 10 | unknown option, a value of the wrong kind, or a command line over the size bound |
| 11 | the --out folder does not exist (reason target-missing), or the target file exists and --overwrite was not given (reason exists) |
| 13 | no space for the archive |

Examples:

```powershell
& .\doc-html-translate.exe report build --out C:\temp\logs.zip; $LASTEXITCODE
```

Expected: 0 and C:\temp\logs.zip exists; 11 when it already did, unless --overwrite is given

```cmd
doc-html-translate.exe -report
```

Expected: exit 0; the path of the archive on its own line (the frozen spelling)

The archive holds the environment summary and as many recent run logs as fit under 15 MiB, newest first, all redacted: no document name, key or personal path. Without --out it is written under the name DIAGNOSTIC-REPORT 8A gives it; with --out at the named file path, or inside an existing folder under the DIAGNOSTIC-REPORT 8A name (rule 9, item P.1, 0.3 item V), created or, with --overwrite, replaced whole through a temporary file. A path ending in a separator is a folder argument and a missing folder is never created. Each run is a new archive. Nothing is sent anywhere. Served by doc-html-translate.exe only.

## `integration add`

Add the right-click "Convert to HTML" entry and the "Open with" entry for every supported file type, without becoming the default handler.

```text
doc-html-translate integration add [--json] [--result <path>]
```

- **Risk:** `writes-user-data` - **cold start:** `oneshot` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** 10000 ms - **idempotent:** yes - **since:** 1.0
- **Forward:** `never` (the process that receives the command does the work itself)
- **Frozen aliases:** `-register-openwith`

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | bool | no | `false` | Print the data as one JSON object. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the data as one JSON file, written whole. |

Data:

| Key | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions` | array | the file types advertised in the Open with list |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | added, or already in place |
| 1 | the registry could not be written, or the result file could not be written |
| 10 | unknown option, a value of the wrong kind, or a command line over the size bound |
| 11 | refused under a Store package, which declares the associations itself (reason packaged); nothing was written |

Examples:

```cmd
doc-html-translate.exe -register-openwith
```

Expected: exit 0; the entries exist (an installer calls this spelling)

```powershell
(& .\doc-html-translate.exe integration add --json | ConvertFrom-Json).extensions
```

Expected: the file types now in the Open with list

Writes per-user keys under HKCU only, needs no elevation and changes no default handler. Started with no arguments the program offers this and default-handler set as two y/N questions, read from standard input by a person at a console, and adds nothing when standard input is closed; that first-run flow is not a verb and keeps its questions. The verb never prompts. Under a Store package the registry is virtualized and the package manifest declares the associations, so the verb is refused (exit 11, reason packaged), never a silent success. Served by doc-html-translate.exe only.

## `default-handler set`

Make the product the default handler for the supported file types, and add the right-click entry.

```text
doc-html-translate default-handler set [--json] [--result <path>]
```

- **Risk:** `writes-user-data` - **cold start:** `oneshot` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** 10000 ms - **idempotent:** yes - **since:** 1.0
- **Forward:** `never` (the process that receives the command does the work itself)
- **Frozen aliases:** `-register`

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | bool | no | `false` | Print the data as one JSON object. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the data as one JSON file, written whole. |

Data:

| Key | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `complete` | bool | every type now opens with the product |
| `default` | array | types the product is now the default for |
| `blocked` | array | types where Windows keeps the app the person chose earlier; only the person can change that |
| `unknown` | array | types whose handler could not be read |
| `failed` | array | types that could not be registered |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | written; data.complete says whether Windows now uses the product for every type |
| 1 | no type could be registered, the right-click entry could not be written, or the result file could not be written |
| 10 | unknown option, a value of the wrong kind, or a command line over the size bound |
| 11 | refused under a Store package, which declares the associations itself (reason packaged); nothing was written |

Examples:

```powershell
(& .\doc-html-translate.exe default-handler set --json | ConvertFrom-Json).blocked
```

Expected: the types Windows keeps for the person's own earlier choice; only the person can change those

```cmd
doc-html-translate.exe -register
```

Expected: exit 0; the frozen spelling also offers Default apps in Settings and waits for Enter, at a console only

Windows protects the person's own choice with a hash no program may forge, so a type the person chose another app for is reported in blocked and never overridden. The verb never opens Settings and never pauses; the frozen spelling -register does both, only while standard output is a terminal. Per-user keys under HKCU only. Under a Store package the verb is refused (exit 11, reason packaged). Served by doc-html-translate.exe only.

## `default-handler release`

Release the default-handler association, leaving the right-click entry and "Open with".

```text
doc-html-translate default-handler release [--json] [--result <path>]
```

- **Risk:** `writes-user-data` - **cold start:** `oneshot` - **wait:** `done` - **time bound:** 10000 ms - **idempotent:** yes - **since:** 1.0
- **Forward:** `never` (the process that receives the command does the work itself)
- **Frozen aliases:** `-unregister`

Options:

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | bool | no | `false` | Print the data as one JSON object. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the data as one JSON file, written whole. |

Data:

| Key | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `released` | array | types released, with the previous handler restored where one was saved |
| `stillDefault` | array | types Windows still opens with the product because the person chose it in Windows itself |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | released, or there was nothing to release |
| 1 | a type could not be released, or the result file could not be written |
| 10 | unknown option, a value of the wrong kind, or a command line over the size bound |
| 11 | refused under a Store package, which declares the associations itself (reason packaged); nothing was written |

Examples:

```cmd
doc-html-translate.exe -unregister
```

Expected: exit 0 (an uninstaller calls this spelling)

```powershell
(& .\doc-html-translate.exe default-handler release --json | ConvertFrom-Json).stillDefault
```

Expected: the types Windows still opens with the product because the person chose it in Windows itself

Gives back the handler saved when the product became the default, or removes the value when none was saved, and touches only the types that point at the product. The right-click entry and Open with stay; nothing here removes them. Under a Store package the verb is refused (exit 11, reason packaged). Served by doc-html-translate.exe only.
